title: Teeth from two caves in southern China point to Denisovans and an unidentified archaic human lineage
tldr: Four fossil teeth from Guangxi caves carry enamel proteins that place a Denisovan-affinity population in subtropical southern China and point to a second archaic human group that matches no known lineage.
byline: Phys.org (CENIEH release), La Brujula Verde, Live Science (via Yahoo News)

title: A bat virus related to RSV can enter human cells in the lab, but antibodies from past RSV infection block it
tldr: A virus found in West African fruit bats and related to RSV entered human cells in laboratory tests, less efficiently than human RSV, and was neutralised by antibodies from people previously exposed to RSV.
byline: German Center for Infection Research (DZIF), Phys.org

title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
tldr: Sequencing the protein-coding genes of more than 1.4 million people implicates 207 genes in adult height, including 17 where a single rare disabling variant shifts height by up to 17 cm.
byline: Jack A. Kosmicki, Liron Ganel, Kyoko Watanabe et al. · Regeneron Genetics Center and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, with cohorts including UK Biobank, Geisinger DiscovEHR

title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
tldr: Pooling three maternal nutrition trials in low-resource settings shows that supplements given to mothers change some breast-milk components, including B vitamins, selenium and fats, while leaving many others unmoved.
byline: Trenton Dailey-Chwalibóg, Andrew Mertens, Kelsey Fehr et al. · University of Manitoba; Ghent University Faculty of Bioscience Engineering; AFRICSante, Burkina Faso; New York University Grossman School of Medicine

title: Health Canada warns of a very rare risk of sudden vision loss with semaglutide drugs
tldr: Health Canada's completed safety review found a possible link between prescription semaglutide and NAION, a form of sudden, usually permanent vision loss, and product labels will be updated.
byline: Health Canada, CBC News via Radio Canada International, Global News

title: Flu admissions in England jump almost 80% in a week, the highest for late November since before Covid
tldr: Hospital admissions for flu in England rose from five to nearly nine per 100,000 people in a week, the highest for this point in November this decade, with vaccination lagging.
byline: BBC News, The Guardian

title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
tldr: An engineered protein glue called TALhesin held chromosome halves together in aged mouse eggs, raising the share of error-free eggs from 46.7% to 74.1%, close to the level in young mice.
byline: Alexandre Webster, Halima Yusuf, Nina Schweizer et al. · Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, Göttingen; eggs donated via Göttingen Fertility Center, Bourn Hall Fertility Clinic (Cambridgeshire) and Fertility Center Berlin

title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
tldr: Structures of a CRISPR-associated transposase revealed how it locks onto a precise genomic target, and redesigned proteins made it 100 times more active without losing on-target specificity.
byline: Shirin Fatma, Shubham Dubey, Vinh H. Truong et al. · St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Department of Structural Biology

title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
tldr: A single-dose CRISPR therapy delivered by one AAV9 vector produced the first molecular evidence of gene editing in the muscles of boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, but one of four participants died.
byline: Guoling Li, Feng Han, Cuijin Wang et al. · HuidaGene Therapeutics (Shanghai), Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

title: The first generic version of the twice-yearly HIV prevention shot lenacapavir arrives in Zambia, at about $40 a year
tldr: The Global Fund says the first generic lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection expected to cost about $40 per person a year, has reached Zambia, with Uganda next.
byline: The Global Fund, BBC, Associated Press (via Yahoo News)

title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases, with only 15% of new cases among known contacts
tldr: Government data show more than 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and most new cases are still appearing outside known chains of transmission.
byline: US CDC, ECDC, Reuters (via Head Topics)

title: Hepatitis B vaccination at birth falls to 65.6% of US newborns, and slips among babies of infected mothers, a records study finds
tldr: An analysis of health records for 1.3 million US infants finds hepatitis B vaccination within a day of birth fell from about 80% in 2022 to 65.6% by June 2026.
byline: Truveta, NEJM Evidence

title: Blood-Pressure–Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum
tldr: Pooling 51 randomized trials and 357,440 people, blood-pressure drugs cut major cardiovascular events by the same relative amount at every level of predicted risk, but the absolute gain shrinks as risk falls.
byline: Zeinab Bidel Milad Nazarzadeh Borislava Mihaylova Qianqian Yang Johan Sundström Nathalie Conrad Dexter Canoy Guyu Zeng David M. Kent William C. Cushman John Chalmers Koon K. Teo Carl J. Pepine Barry R. Davis Mark Woodward and Kazem Rahimithe Blood Pressure Lowering Treatment Trialists’ Collaboration*
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
tldr: Across about 219,000 people in five long-running studies, later-born generations enter old age with better memory and lose it more slowly.
byline: Anders Fjell et al. · University of Oslo

title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
tldr: Enamel proteins from four teeth found in two caves in Guangxi point to two kinds of archaic human in southern China: one Denisovan-like, one that fits no sampled group.
byline: Song Xing, Huiyun Rao, Guangmao Xie et al. · Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Beijing

title: FDA approves bezuclastinib with sunitinib for gastrointestinal stromal tumours after imatinib
tldr: The FDA approved Cogent's Ekitna (bezuclastinib) with sunitinib for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumours after imatinib; in a phase 3 trial the pair held the cancer in check for a median 16.5 months versus 9.2.
byline: Cogent Biosciences (GlobeNewswire release, via WBOC), Pharmaceutical Technology

title: England records 5,258 heat-associated deaths in 2026, the most since monitoring began
tldr: The UK Health Security Agency estimates 5,258 deaths in England were associated with heat between May and September 2026, far above the previous record of 2,985 in 2022.
byline: The Guardian, BBC

title: Dolphins with larger, more predictable social groups live longer, a 40-year study in Shark Bay finds
tldr: Four decades of observations of about 400 wild bottlenose dolphins show that animals that are more sociable and more consistent in the group sizes they keep tend to live longer.
byline: PLOS Biology, University of Queensland, The Guardian

title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
tldr: In 9,476 Brazilians with type 2 diabetes, aiming for systolic blood pressure below 120 instead of below 140 mm Hg did not significantly cut cardiovascular events, and kidney-function declines were more frequent.
byline: Karla Santo Eduardo Martins Gisele S. Silva Patricia O. Guimarães Caio A.M. Tavares João B. Andrade Frederico Monfardini Josué Nieri Silvia R.L. Assis João S. Felício Fábio S. Fuchs and Otavio Berwangerthe OPTIMAL-DIABETES Trial Investigators* · Einstein Hospital Israelita, São Paulo; The George Institute for Global Health, Imperial College London
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: A shared meaning component across languages in the human brain
tldr: Models trained to predict brain responses to one language also predict responses to languages they never saw, across speakers of 21 languages, pointing to a shared representation of meaning.
byline: Andrea Gregor de Varda, Saima Malik-Moraleda, Greta Tuckute et al. · McGovern Institute for Brain Research and Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, MIT

title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
tldr: Imaging of intact vaccinia virus cores shows the virus's gene-copying enzymes parked in pairs beside the genome, next to a channel through the core wall suited to exporting RNA.
byline: Benoît Arragain, Lukas W. Bauer, Victor-Valentin Hodirnau et al. · Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA)

title: FDA approves giredestrant after surgery, the first new hormone therapy for early-stage breast cancer in over 20 years
tldr: The FDA approved Roche's daily pill Wilserdly for early breast cancer after surgery, on the strength of a 4,170-patient trial in which it cut recurrence or death by 30% against standard hormone therapy.
byline: FDA, Fierce Pharma

title: FDA approves ribitol, the first treatment for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
tldr: The FDA approved Welgemda, a twice-daily oral solution, for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 after a 112-patient placebo-controlled trial showed gains in walking speed and lung function at 12 months.
byline: FDA, STAT

title: Kymera's once-daily eczema pill cuts disease severity by 72% in a 244-patient mid-stage trial, the company reports
tldr: In a randomized phase 2b trial, an oral drug that destroys the immune signalling protein STAT6 reduced eczema severity scores by 72% against 27% on placebo; the results are company-reported, not yet peer-reviewed.
byline: Kymera Therapeutics press release (via BioSpace), New Scientist, Dermatology Times

title: CMR to Guide Defibrillator Implantation for LVEF
tldr: In a randomized trial of 353 patients with moderately reduced heart function and scarring on cardiac MRI, implanted defibrillators did not significantly reduce sudden cardiac death or serious arrhythmia over 6.3 years.
byline: Joseph B. Selvanayagam, et al. (CMR GUIDE Investigators) · Flinders University and Flinders Medical Centre, Adelaide

title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
tldr: An implant that runs on the body's own glucose stimulated the vagus nerve whenever its fuel-cell voltage signalled high blood sugar, and lowered blood glucose in diabetic rats over weeks.
byline: Weijun Xiu, Qian Wang, Ling Wan et al. · National University of Singapore

title: FDA rejects Capricor's Duchenne cell therapy a second time, citing unreliable data from its phase 3 trial
tldr: The FDA declined again to approve deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, saying the phase 3 HOPE-3 trial missed its prespecified goals and that inspection findings made its data unreliable.
byline: Pharmacally, NeurologyLive, Capricor (July 2025 release, background)

title: Virginia reports its first measles death of 2026, a young child, as confirmed US cases reach 5,838
tldr: Virginia health officials reported the death of a child aged four or younger who had measles, the 12th such death reported by US states this year, as the CDC's national count reached 5,838 cases.
byline: Virginia Department of Health, CDC, ABC News

title: Merck's antibody-drug conjugate sac-TMT extends survival in heavily pretreated stomach and oesophageal cancer, the company says
tldr: Merck says its 473-patient phase 3 TroFuse-015 trial of sacituzumab tirumotecan met its overall survival goal in third-line gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, but missed on progression-free survival and released no numbers.
byline: BioPharm International, OncoDaily, The Pharma Letter

title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis
tldr: A platform trial in 401 adults with tuberculosis screened ten new four-drug combinations at once and selected two 16-week regimens, each built around a new drug, for further testing.
byline: Hanif Esmail Nicholas I. Paton Jodie A. Schildkraut Ilaria Motta Alexander J. Szubert Suzanne M. Dufault Norbert Heinrich Simon Tiberi Cissy M. Kityo Timothy D. McHugh Fairoez Ryklief Daniela M. Cirillo Rodney Dawson Karen Sanders Stellah Mpagama Lindsay C. Thompson Le Hong Van Dominic Wakerley Elena Tudor Angela M. Crook Patrick P.J. Phillips Guy Thwaites Christoph Lange Martin J. Boeree Gareth Maher-Edwards Natasa Lazarevic Jolanda E. van de Logt Derek J. Sloan David Barros-Aguirre and Michael Hoelscherthe PARADIGM4TB (UNITE4TB-01) Trial Team* · University College London; Radboud University Medical Center; National University of Singapore; LMU University Hospital Munich; GSK
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Multiscale spatial atlas of human basal ganglia cell types and communities
tldr: A spatial map of about 7.9 million cells in four human brains resolves 60 cell types in the basal ganglia and shows how they are arranged, part of a 26-study atlas of the region.
byline: Bereket Tesfay Berackey, Zhiqun Tan, Ginny Wu et al. · University of California, Irvine

title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
tldr: Three cryo-electron microscopy structures show that the hormone relaxin-2 and a small-molecule drug candidate, AZD5462, switch on the same receptor by binding different parts of it and reshaping it differently.
byline: James Osei-Owusu, Tristan Girbau, Xunan Wang et al. · Harvard Medical School

title: A blood protein flags advanced CTE in former football players, a small JAMA study finds
tldr: In 21 former football players who later donated their brains, blood levels of a tau protein fragment were far higher in those with advanced CTE, a preliminary step toward diagnosing the disease in life.
byline: The Boston Globe, AZFamily

title: FDA approves Regeneron's Livsayis, the first gene-silencing drug for generalized myasthenia gravis
tldr: The FDA approved cemdisiran (Livsayis), an injection given four times a year that silences production of the immune protein C5, for adults with antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis.
byline: Medical Daily, WebMD, BioPharm International

title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
tldr: Recordings from 28 surgical patients show a small spot in Wernicke's area, long seen as a listening region, activates about a quarter-second before each spoken word and is needed for speaking.
byline: Alexander B. Silva, Matthew K. Leonard, Patrick W. Hullett et al. · University of California, San Francisco

title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
tldr: Teeth from two caves in Guangxi, dated to between about 324,000 and 184,000 years ago, show Homo erectus survived in southern China's rainforests much later than its previously known disappearance from mainland Asia.
byline: Wei Liao, Clément Zanolli, Ragnheiður Diljá Ásmundsdóttir et al.

title: A daily KRAS-blocking pill plus chemotherapy stops tumour growth in 90% of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer in an early trial
tldr: In a 61-patient phase 1/2 trial, daraxonrasib plus standard chemotherapy shrank tumours in just over 60% of people newly diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; 76.6% were alive at one year.
byline: BBC News, The Guardian

title: FDA grants accelerated approval to GSK's Nelkarmi for ALK-positive lung cancer that has outgrown earlier drugs
tldr: The FDA cleared neladalkib, a daily pill, for advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer after earlier ALK inhibitors stop working, based on response rates of 49% and 32% in a 222-patient trial.
byline: pharmaphorum, chemXplore

title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
tldr: In two phase 3 trials with 1,019 adults with obesity and painful knee osteoarthritis, weekly retatrutide injections cut pain scores and body weight significantly more than placebo, with more serious side effects.
byline: Thomas J. Schnitzer David J. Hunter Philip G. Conaghan Arya M. Sharma Sue D. Pedersen Kaiyi Chen So Young Park Nune Makarova Kathryn Giblin and Tammy Forresterthe TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA Investigators* · Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine; University of Sydney; University of Leeds; University of Alberta; University of Calgary; Eli Lilly and Company
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis
tldr: A DNA recorder inserted into a fertilized mouse egg wrote an ordered log of cell divisions into the genome, letting researchers rebuild a mouse embryo's cell family tree from the first division to organ formation.
byline: Qi Yu, Haedong Kim, Sophie Seidel et al. · University of Washington School of Medicine; Howard Hughes Medical Institute; Dartmouth College

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals molecular organization of human and nonhuman primate basal ganglia
tldr: Mapping where each cell type sits in the basal ganglia of humans, macaques and marmosets, researchers found a highly stereotyped layout shared across primates and often with mice, with gene gradients laid over discrete compartments.
byline: Madeleine N. Hewitt, Meghan A. Turner, Nelson Johansen et al. · Allen Institute for Brain Science; Princeton Neuroscience Institute; Leiden University Medical Center; Delft University of Technology; The Rockefeller University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Washington University in St. Louis; RIKEN; Kyoto University; University of Washington

title: FDA approves venglustat, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease
tldr: The FDA approved Sanofi's Infilbray (venglustat), a daily pill that reaches the brain, after a 43-patient randomized trial showed better neurological scores than standard enzyme infusions at one year.
byline: FDA

title: An off-the-shelf leukemia vaccine extends survival by nine months in a phase 3 trial, its developers report
tldr: In the 126-patient REGAL trial, people with acute myeloid leukemia in second remission who got the WT1 peptide vaccine galinpepimut-S lived a median 24.0 months, against 14.7 months on other treatments.
byline: Memorial Sloan Kettering, BioPharm International

title: Biogen's tau-lowering drug diranersen shows larger effects at two years in early Alzheimer's, in an open-label extension
tldr: Biogen says the twice-yearly 60 mg dose of diranersen slowed decline on the CDR-SB dementia scale by 38% at two years, up from 26% at 18 months, though the comparison comes from an open-label extension.
byline: Biogen (GlobeNewswire), ReachMD

title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
tldr: Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China, dated 324,000 to 184,000 years ago, carry chemical signs of a dense rainforest diet and of long journeys in childhood.
byline: K. E. Westaway, R. Joannes-Boyau, W. Liao et al. · Macquarie University, Southern Cross University, Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Vertebrate Palaeontology and Palaeoanthropology

title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
tldr: Mining 85,123 genetic datasets, researchers found egoviruses, the closest known relatives of poxviruses, in the guts of humans and livestock worldwide, hinting that the smallpox family began in animal guts.
byline: Morgan Gaïa, Ulysse Guyet, Hans-Joachim Ruscheweyh et al. · French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS)

title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease: The NOPARK Randomized Clinical Trial
tldr: In a 410-person Norwegian trial, a year of the NAD-boosting supplement nicotinamide riboside did not help early Parkinson's disease; symptom scores were slightly worse than with placebo.
byline: NOPARK trial investigators (study director: Charalampos Tzoulis) · Haukeland University Hospital, University of Bergen

title: FDA approves adrabetadex, the first drug shown to lengthen survival in infantile-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C
tldr: The FDA approved Lembaz (adrabetadex), a spinal injection given every two weeks, after treated patients with early-onset Niemann-Pick disease type C lived a median 8.5 years versus 4.9 years in matched controls.
byline: FDA

title: AriBio's oral Alzheimer's drug AR1001 slows decline in patients taking no other dementia drug, but not in its full phase 3 trial
tldr: In a 1,535-patient phase 3 trial, the daily pill AR1001 slowed decline by 31% among 604 patients on no other dementia drug, meeting a prespecified goal, but showed no significant effect overall.
byline: MoneyToday, iNews24

title: Nicotinamide Riboside for Patients With Early-Stage Parkinson Disease
tldr: In a 410-person randomized trial, a year of the NAD-boosting supplement nicotinamide riboside did not slow early Parkinson's disease; symptom scores ended slightly worse than with placebo.
byline: Charalampos Tzoulis and the NOPARK investigators · University of Bergen; Haukeland University Hospital

title: FDA approves giredestrant, a Roche pill for advanced breast cancer with ESR1 mutations
tldr: The FDA approved Roche's giredestrant (Wilserdly) with everolimus for advanced ER-positive breast cancer carrying an ESR1 mutation, after a trial showed a longer delay before the cancer worsened.
byline: Genentech (press release via Yahoo Finance), Medical Daily, STAT

title: A bladder-instilled immunotherapy cut cancer recurrence by 68% in a phase 3 trial, CG Oncology reports
tldr: In a 367-patient randomized trial, CG Oncology's cretostimogene lowered the risk of bladder cancer returning after surgery by 68% compared with monitoring alone, according to topline company results.
byline: Quiver Quantitative (summary of CG Oncology press release), PharmaShots, STAT

title: CDC scientists count 112 measles infections in pregnancy and 13 babies born with measles since 2025
tldr: A preliminary CDC analysis in NEJM Evidence documents 112 confirmed measles cases in pregnant women and 13 newborns with congenital measles in the United States since the start of 2025.
byline: The New York Times, NBC News (Associated Press), Associated Press via KSLA

title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
tldr: In a two-year randomized trial of 167 children aged 6 to 11 with obesity, weekly semaglutide lowered BMI by 13.5% at 68 weeks while it rose 2.7% on placebo; stomach side effects were common.
byline: Ania M. Jastreboff Nina M. Harder-Lauridsen Michelle Van Name Antje Körner Aaron S. Kelly Daniel Weghuber Jens-Christian Holm Christine Frithioff-Bøjsøe Shilpa Middolu Tina Buch and Martin Wabitschthe STEP Young Investigators* · Yale University School of Medicine; Ulm University Medical Center; University of Leipzig
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
tldr: Tested in 844,108 adults in four countries, a definition of obesity that adds waist measures and organ function to BMI separated people at high risk of death from those at modest risk.
byline: An Pan, Shengping Yang, Rafael Ramos et al. · King's College London; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Kailuan General Hospital; North China University of Science and Technology; Pennington Biomedical Research Center; University of Colorado Anschutz; University of Girona; Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore

title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
tldr: Stone points from a 125,000-year-old lakeshore in Saudi Arabia's Empty Quarter carry residues suggesting they were mounted on shafts and possibly tipped with plant poison.
byline: Chris Clarkson, Gilbert J. Price, Amir Kalifi et al. · Griffith University; King Abdullah University of Science and Technology; Saudi Heritage Commission

title: FDA declines to approve ivonescimab for lung cancer because the trial did not show a significant survival gain
tldr: The FDA rejected Summit's ivonescimab plus chemotherapy for previously treated EGFR-mutated lung cancer, saying slower tumor progression without a statistically significant survival benefit was not enough.
byline: The New York Times, Reuters (via SRN News), OncoDaily

title: The US has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, people close to the Pan American Health Organization's review say
tldr: An expert commission reporting to the Pan American Health Organization has concluded that measles is again spreading continuously in the US, ending a status held since 2000, according to people familiar with the review.
byline: CNN, KFF Health News (via NPR)

title: Six months in, Congo's Ebola outbreak still adds up to 500 cases a week as attacks on health workers disrupt the response
tldr: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak centered on the Democratic Republic of the Congo has passed 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths, and WHO and UN officials say armed violence is now blocking containment.
byline: CIDRAP, ECDC, CDC

title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement
tldr: In a trial of 18,883 joint replacement patients, aspirin was not shown to prevent clots and deaths as well as rivaroxaban or warfarin, which in turn were not shown to be as safe.
byline: Vincent D. Pellegrini Carol A. Lambourne Laurence S. Magder Patricia D. Franklin Jay S. Magaziner Brook I. Martin Richard Iorio Kevin L. Garvin Michael A. Mont Wayne E. Moschetti Antonia F. Francisthe PEPPER Trial Investigators and the Steering Committee of the PEPPER Trial* · Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center and Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth; University of Maryland School of Medicine; Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine; University of Utah; Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Single-cell, multi-region profiling of the macaque brain across the lifespan
tldr: An atlas of 5.3 million cells from 11 brain regions of 55 rhesus macaques charts how each cell type changes with age and finds overlap with the molecular signatures of Alzheimer's disease.
byline: Wei Yang, Kelsi L. Watkins, Alex R. DeCasien et al. · University of Washington; Arizona State University; National Institute on Aging; University of Pennsylvania; University of Alabama at Birmingham; Caribbean Primate Research Center, University of Puerto Rico

title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
tldr: Fruit flies evolving in outdoor and indoor cages changed pigmentation in a direction a genetic map could predict, but which genes did the changing was largely unpredictable.
byline: J. A. Smiley-Rhodes, M. C. Bitter, S. Berardi et al. · Stanford University; University of Pennsylvania; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub

title: FDA approves durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin around surgery for bladder cancer patients who cannot take cisplatin
tldr: The FDA approved an immunotherapy plus antibody-drug conjugate given before and after bladder removal for patients who cannot or will not take cisplatin, after a 695-patient trial showed longer event-free and overall survival.
byline: FDA, The ASCO Post

title: US measles deaths climb as the CDC's tally reaches six and states report ten, with cases above 5,400
tldr: The CDC now counts six US measles deaths in 2026 while state health departments report ten, cases have reached 5,412, and a regional health body is weighing whether the US has lost measles-elimination status.
byline: CIDRAP, PolitiFact

title: China approves Lilly's orforglipron, the first GLP-1 weight-loss pill cleared there
tldr: China's drug regulator approved Eli Lilly's orforglipron tablets for adults with obesity, or overweight plus a related condition, making it the first oral GLP-1 drug for weight management in the country.
byline: Pharmaceutical Technology, Plataforma Media

title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
tldr: In a non-randomized Dutch study of 231 young adults in refractory cardiac arrest, helicopter teams starting ECMO on scene saw 40% survive to discharge versus 20% with conventional care.
byline: Dinis Reis Miranda Xavier Moors Samir Ali Iscander M. Maissan Hans L. van Schuppen Lars Mommers Ellen E.M. Weelink Robert-Jan Houmes Fabian O. Kooij Marijn Tacken Manfred J. venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
tldr: A small DNA switch that controls the gene DACH1, with a feature shared among primates, helps the developing cortex make more of a special stem cell abundant in primate brains, in organoids and mice.
byline: Pei-Shan Hou, Ching-Yu Chuang, Feng-Lan Chiu et al. · National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University; Academia Sinica; Kyoto University

title: A multi-tissue atlas of genetic regulatory effects in sheep
tldr: SheepGTEx maps how DNA variants control gene activity across 51 sheep tissues and cell types, and ancient DNA shows breeding favored variants acting in just one or a few tissues, such as skin.
byline: Mian Gong, Ziyang Zhuang, Xiangrong Sun et al. · Aarhus University

title: The American Cancer Society now recommends regular PSA screening for prostate cancer, every two years from age 50
tldr: The American Cancer Society's new guideline recommends a PSA blood test every two years for average-risk men aged 50 to 69, and yearly from 45 for Black men and men with strong family history.
byline: American Cancer Society, The New York Times

title: FDA approves pimicotinib, a once-daily pill, for joint tumors that are hard to remove surgically
tldr: The FDA approved EMD Serono's pimicotinib for symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor after a placebo-controlled trial in which 56% of treated patients responded, against 3.2% on placebo.
byline: FDA, HMP Global Oncology

title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
tldr: In a phase 3 trial of 1,137 people with resected high-risk melanoma, adding a personalized mRNA therapy to pembrolizumab raised two-year recurrence-free survival from 70.0% to 82.2%.
byline: Georgina V. Long Muhammad A. Khattak Helen J. Gogas Dirk Schadendorf Ana Arance Matteo S. Carlino Piotr Rutkowski Gareth Rivalland Antoni Ribas Janice M. Mehnert Patrick A. Ascierto and Michele Del Vecchiothe INTerpath-001 Investigators* · Melanoma Institute Australia
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Cross-species multiomic atlas of the primate basal ganglia
tldr: A cell-by-cell atlas of 1.8 million nuclei from human, macaque and marmoset basal ganglia finds 61 cell types conserved over 76 million years and maps psychiatric and neurodegenerative risk onto specific cells.
byline: Nelson J. Johansen, Yuanyuan Fu, Matthew Schmitz et al. · Allen Institute

title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
tldr: In mice, the gut antibody IgA slows the renewal of the colon lining through a surface protein called DMBT1, and its absence raises susceptibility to colorectal tumors.
byline: Gregory P. Donaldson, Gabriella Lima dos Reis, Marwa Saad et al. · The Rockefeller University

title: Beam's base-edited sickle cell therapy keeps patients free of severe pain crises for a year in its pivotal trial
tldr: Beam Therapeutics says its one-time base-edited cell therapy, risto-cel, met its main goal of 12 months without severe pain crises in a 49-patient single-arm trial, and plans a US filing.
byline: PharmaShots (summary of Beam's press release), BioPharm International

title: A Lancet Psychiatry analysis compares how well 21 antidepressants keep depression at bay over months to years
tldr: Pooling 115 studies longer than 12 weeks, researchers found escitalopram, duloxetine and agomelatine somewhat more likely than fluoxetine to bring lasting improvement; experts call the differences modest.
byline: The New York Times, BBC News

title: Everyone in a 100,000-person All of Us sample carries gene variants that affect medicines, and a quarter got an affected drug
tldr: A Pitt-led analysis of nearly 100,000 genomes found every participant carried at least one drug-relevant variant (median nine), 24.4% had been prescribed an affected drug, and over 17,000 variants were new.
byline: University of Pittsburgh via Medical Xpress, STAT, Science Translational Medicine

title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
tldr: In lab-grown human neurons lacking the ALS protein TDP-43, fixing one splicing error in the synapse gene UNC13A with an antisense drug restored communication between neurons.
byline: Matthew J. Keuss, Peter Harley, Eugeni Ryadnov et al. · King's College London; University College London; Francis Crick Institute; Leibniz-FMP; Trace Neuroscience

title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
tldr: Yearly stored blood samples show that in two-thirds of women who later got acute myeloid leukaemia, the first driver mutation arose before age 20, and mutant clones then grew predictably.
byline: Caroline J. Watson, Gladys Y. P. Poon, Hamish A. J. MacGregor et al. · University of Cambridge; University College London

title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
tldr: GPS-tracked tapirs and giant anteaters in Brazil carried more microplastics in their blood when their home ranges held more human disturbance or lay nearer waste facilities.
byline: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz, Arnaud L. J. Desbiez, Mario Henrique Alves et al. · University of British Columbia (Kelowna); Center for Advanced Systems Understanding (CASUS), Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf

title: FDA orders a rare optic-nerve warning on all GLP-1 drugs
tldr: The FDA will require every GLP-1 medicine to carry a warning of a potential increased risk of NAION, a rare condition that can cause permanent vision loss in one eye.
byline: FDA, CBS News

title: FDA approves asundexian, the first factor XIa blocker, to prevent a second stroke
tldr: The FDA approved Bayer's once-daily pill Sunharbo (asundexian) alongside antiplatelet therapy after a mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic stroke or high-risk TIA, after a 12,327-person trial showed a 26% lower risk of ischemic stroke.
byline: FDA, pharmaphorum

title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
tldr: In 4,368 people with prior stroke or TIA, aiming for systolic blood pressure under 120 mm Hg rather than 140 cut major cardiovascular events by 21%, at the cost of more kidney-function events.
byline: Gisele Sampaio Silva M. Julia Machline-Carrion Karla Santo João Brainer Clares de Andrade Eduardo Martins Patrícia Oliveira Guimarães Frederico Monfardini Josué Nieri Silvia R.L. venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease
tldr: Monthly ziltivekimab, an IL-6 antibody, sharply cut inflammatory markers in 6,376 people with atherosclerosis and kidney disease but did not change heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death.
byline: Paul M Ridker A. Michael Lincoff Nikolaus Marx Ann Marie Navar Naveed Sattar Katherine R. Tuttle Matthew Budoff Morten Böttcher Matthew A. Cavender Robin P. Choudhury Jan H. Engelmann Sofia Gerward G. Kees Hovingh Anders Hvelplund and Vlado Perkovicthe ZEUS Investigators* · Brigham and Women's Hospital; Mass General Brigham
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: A single–amino acid difference between rodent and human Andes virus affects viral glycoprotein trafficking
tldr: One amino acid differs between rodent and human Andes virus glycoproteins, and swapping it changed how long the protein stays in the Golgi and how fast virus-like particles are released in human cells.
byline: Santiago Vidal-Freire, Natalia M. Ferressini-Gerpe, Carla M. Bellomo et al. · Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; Administración Nacional de Laboratorios e Institutos de Salud Dr. Carlos G. Malbrán (ANLIS); Centro Ciencia y Vida and Universidad San Sebastián; U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases; National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

title: Lp(a)-lowering drug pelacarsen cuts the target by 78% but not heart attacks or strokes, in a large phase 3 trial
tldr: In Lp(a)HORIZON, pelacarsen lowered lipoprotein(a) by about 78% in over 8,300 people with heart disease, yet heart attacks, strokes and cardiovascular deaths occurred at the same rate as on placebo.
byline: American Heart Association, Healio, American College of Cardiology

title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
tldr: In a randomized trial of about 1,880 adults over 70 without heart disease, stopping statins was statistically noninferior over two years, but cardiovascular events were more frequent over longer follow-up.
byline: Nicolas Rodondi Moa Lina Haller Julia Bianca Bardoczi Luise Adam Manuel Raphael Blum Baris Gencer Tamar Itach Julian Simon Flury Lara Aurora Brockhus Philipp Stefan Aebi Martin Feller Claudia Gregoriano Roxane de la Harpe Jacobijn Gussekloo Nathalie Schwab Pierre Poulizac Simon Pieter Mooijaart Jürg-Hans Beer Stéphanie Baggio Sebastian Carballo Fabrice Bonnet Dina Zekry Luca Gabutti Maria Monika Wertli Drahomir Aujesky Douglas Charles Bauer Rita Fran Redberg Philip Greenland Rosalinde Klazina Elisabeth Poortvliet Philipp Schuetz Marie Méan Alan Gary Haynes and Sven Trellethe STREAM Investigators*
venue: The New England Journal of Medicine

title: Noise pollution alters the body or behavior of 80% of animal species studied, a Science analysis finds
tldr: A pooled analysis of 214 experiments on 177 species found human-made noise changed physiology or behavior in eight of ten species and cut animal numbers by about 37% in noisy areas.
byline: Phys.org, Science (study DOI)

title: Parkinson's may be driven by a vicious cycle that clogs the brain's waste drainage
tldr: Misfolded alpha-synuclein appears to inflame the lymphatic vessels that drain the brain, which then clear it less well, in human tissue and mice.
byline: New Scientist, Journal of Experimental Medicine (study)

title: FDA grants accelerated approval to a subcutaneous antibody for previously treated head and neck cancer
tldr: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after chemotherapy and immunotherapy, based on a 42% response rate in 102 patients.
byline: FDA, Johnson & Johnson (OrigAMI-4 results release)

title: A hair and 1,000 seeds from a Siberian tomb give the oldest directly dated evidence of cannabis intoxication
tldr: Archaeologists found about 1,000 cannabis seeds and hair carrying a breakdown product of THC in a Scythian princely tomb in Siberia, dated to the early eighth century B.C., in a study in Science.
byline: University of Bern, New Scientist, Scientific American

title: British health worker with Ebola flown home as the Congo outbreak passes 10,000 cases
tldr: A British healthcare worker infected in DR Congo is being evacuated to the UK, the first British case of an outbreak that has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and has no approved treatment.
byline: The Guardian, ECDC

title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
tldr: Researchers built the largest map yet of how essential genes interact in the tuberculosis bacterium, finding nearly 6,500 interactions that could guide new drug targets and antibiotic combinations.
byline: Isaac J. Kresse, Natalie Y. Sayegh, Vanisha Munsamy-Govender et al. · Rockefeller University

title: The global geography of threats to freshwater biodiversity
tldr: A global analysis of 45 threats to more than 21,000 freshwater species finds farming, dams and agricultural runoff dominate, and that freshwater species face higher threat on average than land species.
byline: Christophe Brabant, Laura Pollock, Jonas Geldmann et al. · McGill University

title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial
tldr: A large international randomized trial found no evidence that prone positioning or high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improves ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome.
byline: Martha A Q Curley, Martin C J Kneyber, Ira M Cheifetz et al.

title: First measles death in New York State in 30 years
tldr: A child in Lewis County, New York, died of measles, the state's first measles death in 30 years, as US cases reach their highest level in about 35 years.
byline: The Guardian, CIDRAP, Gothamist

title: FDA finalizes potency guidance for cell and gene therapies
tldr: The FDA issued final guidance telling makers of cell and gene therapies to build a plan proving that every batch is potent before it reaches a patient.
byline: FDA

title: English A&Es to use early warning scores for sick children
tldr: NHS England is introducing a vital-signs scoring system for children in emergency departments this winter, with parents' concerns able to trigger urgent review regardless of score.
byline: The Guardian, BBC News

title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
tldr: In a randomized trial of 744 older adults with moderate aortic stenosis and risk features, early valve replacement cut two-year death or heart failure events from 23.9% to 16.7%.
byline: Philippe Généreux Raj R. Makkar Philippe Pibarot Jeroen J. Bax Brian R. Lindman Kamran Muhammad J. Bradley Oldemeyer Mark Pirwitz Colin M. Barker Vinod H. Thourani Pradeep K.
